highlights_headline: SkiaSharp 4.159.0 adopts Skia m159 and raises the WebAssembly minimum to .NET 9.
highlights_body: The engine update brings WebAssembly SIMD CPU rasterization, Windows font-loading improvements, and image and rendering fixes. Non-WebAssembly .NET 8 support remains unchanged.

breaking.title: Move .NET 8 WebAssembly apps to a supported toolchain
breaking.body: SkiaSharp and HarfBuzzSharp no longer provide .NET 8 WebAssembly native assets; unsupported WASM target frameworks now fail before building. Retarget WASM apps to .NET 9 or later and use runtime-matched archives: .NET 9/10 use Emscripten 3.1.56, while .NET 11+ uses 6.0.2. These archives are not interchangeable with older .NET toolchains. Non-WASM .NET 8 support is unchanged.

bullets.detail: Updates the native renderer with WebAssembly SIMD CPU rasterization, Windows font-loading improvements, and image and rendering correctness fixes. Public managed signatures remain unchanged.

The shared HashCode polyfill now seeds from the operating system random-number generator. Hash codes remain randomized per process and stable within a process; first use now loads System.Security.Cryptography, adding initialization cost.

contributor_summaries.rolfbjarne: Replaced the shared HashCode seed with OS-generated randomness and added analyzer safeguards for shipped code.
